# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sayadi_2026_dalbavancin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sayadi_2026_dalbavancin"))$description`
* Article: [Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2026;70(8):e00665-26](https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00665-26)

Dalbavancin is a long-acting lipoglycopeptide approved for acute bacterial skin
and skin structure infection and used off-label in repeated 1500 mg doses for
bone, joint and endovascular infections that need weeks of therapy. Sayadi 2026
fitted a population PK model to routine therapeutic-drug-monitoring (TDM) data
from 183 patients at Limoges University Hospital, validated it externally in 30
patients from Nantes, benchmarked it against five published dalbavancin models
(Carrothers 2020, Cojutti 2023 x2, Chiriac 2024 and Baiardi 2025) and a model
average, and used Monte Carlo simulation to estimate how long a two-dose regimen
keeps the probability of target attainment (PTA) for fAUC24/MIC >= 111.1 above
90%.

Only the model developed in the paper is packaged here. The five comparator
models are the published models of other authors (several are already in
nlmixr2lib, e.g. `Carrothers_2020_dalbavancin`, `Chiriac_2024_dalbavancin`,
`Baiardi_2025_dalbavancin`), and the model average is a per-patient weighting of
Bayesian posterior predictions, not a population model.

# Population

The development data set comprised 183 adults contributing 406 total plasma
dalbavancin concentrations, all above the 0.5 mg/L LLOQ (Sayadi 2026 Table 2).
The cohort was elderly (median age 77 years, IQR 67-83, range 23-99) and 62.8%
male. Median body weight was 79 kg (IQR 65-88, range 32-138) and median CKD-EPI
eGFR 75 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (IQR 49-87, range 14-135). Patients received 1 to 23
doses (24.6% received three or more) with 1 to 25 TDM samples each, collected
mostly at trough and in the late elimination phase. The main indications were
osteoarticular infection (43.2%) and infective endocarditis (12.6%). Missing
weights (n = 27) and creatinine values (n = 29) were imputed by k-nearest
neighbours before fitting.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Sayadi_2026_dalbavancin")()$population`.

# Virtual cohort

The paper's Monte Carlo design (Results, Monte Carlo simulations) stratifies
patients two ways: by eGFR (15-29, 30-59, 60-89 and 90-120 mL/min/1.73 m^2) at
the median weight of 79 kg, and by weight (30-49, 50-79, 80-119 and 120-200 kg)
at the median eGFR of 75 mL/min/1.73 m^2. Each stratum receives 1500 mg on day 1
and day 8 (D1/D8) or on day 1 and day 15 (D1/D15) as 30-minute infusions, and is
followed for 100 days. The paper used 10,000 virtual patients per stratum; 200
per stratum are used here, which resolves the day on which PTA falls below 90%
to within a day or two.

```{r cohort}
mod <- readModelDb("Sayadi_2026_dalbavancin")
# PTA is computed from the individual (error-free) unbound profile.
mod_sim <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod, which = "sigma")

set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)

n_per_stratum <- 200L
strata <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    cov = "eGFR", stratum = c("15-29", "30-59", "60-89", "90-120"),
    lo = c(15, 30, 60, 90), hi = c(29, 59, 89, 120)
  ),
  tibble::tibble(
    cov = "Weight", stratum = c("30-49", "50-79", "80-119", "120-200"),
    lo = c(30, 50, 80, 120), hi = c(49, 79, 119, 200)
  )
)
regimens <- c("D1/D8", "D1/D15")
second_day <- c("D1/D8" = 8, "D1/D15" = 15)

# One row per virtual patient: the stratified covariate is drawn uniformly
# within its stratum, the other covariate is held at the cohort median.
cohort <- tidyr::expand_grid(regimen = regimens, strata) |>
  dplyr::slice(rep(seq_len(dplyr::n()), each = n_per_stratum)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    x = stats::runif(dplyr::n(), lo, hi),
    CRCL = ifelse(cov == "eGFR", x, 75),
    WT = ifelse(cov == "Weight", x, 79)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(id, regimen, cov, stratum, CRCL, WT)

cohort |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, cov, stratum) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(), CRCL = median(CRCL), WT = median(WT),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Simulation

```{r sim-helpers}
hours_per_day <- 24
obs_grid <- seq(0, 100 * hours_per_day, by = 2)

# Event table: 1500 mg 30-minute infusions at the times (h) in the
# `dose_times` list column, observations on the central compartment on a 2-h
# grid plus 30 min after each dose so the trapezoid captures the
# end-of-infusion peak.
make_events <- function(cohort) {
  doses <- cohort |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = dose_times) |>
    tidyr::unnest(time) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = 1500, rate = 3000, cmt = "central")
  obs <- cohort |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = lapply(dose_times, function(d) sort(unique(c(obs_grid, d + 0.5))))) |>
    tidyr::unnest(time) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, CRCL, WT)
}

# Unbound AUC over each calendar day (day 1 = 0-24 h) by the linear trapezoid,
# as in the paper (pracma trapezoidal integration).
daily_fauc <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Ccu) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time) |>
    dplyr::group_by(id) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      seg = (Ccu + dplyr::lead(Ccu)) / 2 * (dplyr::lead(time) - time),
      day = floor(time / hours_per_day) + 1
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(seg), day <= 100) |>
    dplyr::group_by(id, day) |>
    dplyr::summarise(fauc24 = sum(seg), .groups = "drop")
}

# Population PTA per day for the two MICs.
pta_by_day <- function(fauc, cohort, mic = c(0.125, 0.25)) {
  fauc |>
    dplyr::inner_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
    tidyr::expand_grid(mic = mic) |>
    dplyr::group_by(regimen, cov, stratum, mic, day) |>
    dplyr::summarise(pta = mean(fauc24 / mic >= 111.1), .groups = "drop")
}

# First day on or after `from_day` on which PTA is below 90%; 100 when PTA
# never falls below 90% within the 100-day horizon.
critical_day <- function(pta, from_day) {
  pta |>
    dplyr::inner_join(from_day, by = c("regimen", "cov", "stratum", "mic")) |>
    dplyr::group_by(regimen, cov, stratum, mic) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      crit = if (any(day >= from & pta < 0.9)) min(day[day >= from & pta < 0.9]) else 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

```{r sim-two-dose}
two_dose <- cohort |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose_times = lapply(regimen, function(r) c(0, (second_day[[r]] - 1) * hours_per_day)))
ev2 <- make_events(two_dose)

sim2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_sim, ev2, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(all(sim2$Ccu >= 0))

pta2 <- pta_by_day(daily_fauc(sim2), cohort)
from2 <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  tibble::tibble(regimen = regimens, from = unname(second_day[regimens])),
  dplyr::distinct(strata, cov, stratum),
  mic = c(0.125, 0.25)
)
crit2 <- critical_day(pta2, from2)
```

The paper then adds a third 1500 mg dose at the point where PTA drops below
90% in each stratum. Here the third dose is given at the end of the stratum's
simulated critical day, which reproduces the brief dip below 90% visible in
Figures 2B, 2D, 2F and 2H of the paper.

```{r sim-three-dose}
three_dose <- cohort |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(mic = c(0.125, 0.25)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(crit2, by = c("regimen", "cov", "stratum", "mic")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    dose_times = Map(function(r, c) c(0, (second_day[[r]] - 1) * hours_per_day, c * hours_per_day), regimen, crit)
  )
ev3 <- make_events(three_dose)
sim3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_sim, ev3, returnType = "data.frame")

pta3 <- daily_fauc(sim3) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(three_dose, id, regimen, cov, stratum, mic, crit), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::group_by(regimen, cov, stratum, mic, day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pta = mean(fauc24 / mic >= 111.1), .groups = "drop")
crit3 <- critical_day(pta3, dplyr::rename(crit2, from = crit) |> dplyr::mutate(from = from + 1))
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 2 - PTA over time at an MIC of 0.25 mg/L

```{r fig2, fig.height = 7}
fig_pta <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(pta2, doses = "2 doses"),
  dplyr::mutate(pta3, doses = "3 doses")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    stratum = factor(stratum, levels = unique(strata$stratum)),
    panel = paste(regimen, "|", cov, "|", doses),
    panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel[order(match(regimen, regimens), cov == "Weight", doses)]))
  )

ggplot(dplyr::filter(fig_pta, mic == 0.25), aes(day / 7, 100 * pta, colour = stratum)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "PTA (%)", colour = "Stratum",
    title = "PTA of fAUC24/MIC >= 111.1 at MIC 0.25 mg/L",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Sayadi 2026 (eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m^2, weight in kg)."
  )
```

## Table S1 - day on which PTA falls below 90%

Table S1 of the paper lists, per regimen and stratum, the day on which PTA
first falls below 90% after the two-dose regimen (the day the third dose is
due) and after the third dose (the day a fourth dose would be due).

```{r tableS1}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen, ~cov, ~stratum, ~d3_0125, ~d3_025, ~d4_0125, ~d4_025,
  "D1/D15", "Weight", "120-200", 34, 26, 57, 40,
  "D1/D15", "Weight", "30-49", 50, 41, 83, 66,
  "D1/D15", "Weight", "50-79", 50, 37, 83, 60,
  "D1/D15", "Weight", "80-119", 45, 29, 76, 48,
  "D1/D15", "eGFR", "15-29", 64, 48, 100, 79,
  "D1/D15", "eGFR", "30-59", 56, 41, 94, 68,
  "D1/D15", "eGFR", "60-89", 51, 36, 85, 60,
  "D1/D15", "eGFR", "90-120", 47, 34, 78, 55,
  "D1/D8", "Weight", "120-200", 29, 20, 52, 34,
  "D1/D8", "Weight", "30-49", 45, 36, 78, 61,
  "D1/D8", "Weight", "50-79", 45, 32, 79, 56,
  "D1/D8", "Weight", "80-119", 40, 24, 71, 43,
  "D1/D8", "eGFR", "15-29", 59, 44, 100, 76,
  "D1/D8", "eGFR", "30-59", 51, 36, 89, 63,
  "D1/D8", "eGFR", "60-89", 46, 32, 80, 55,
  "D1/D8", "eGFR", "90-120", 43, 29, 74, 50
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(starts_with("d"), names_to = "key", values_to = "published") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dose = ifelse(substr(key, 2, 2) == "3", "3rd dose due", "4th dose due"),
    mic = ifelse(grepl("0125", key), 0.125, 0.25)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-key)

simulated <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(crit2, dose = "3rd dose due"),
  dplyr::mutate(crit3, dose = "4th dose due")
)

chk <- published |>
  dplyr::inner_join(simulated, by = c("regimen", "cov", "stratum", "mic", "dose")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff_days = crit - published)
stopifnot(nrow(chk) == 64L)

chk |>
  dplyr::arrange(dose, mic, regimen, cov) |>
  dplyr::select(dose, mic, regimen, cov, stratum, published, crit, diff_days) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose" = dose, "MIC (mg/L)" = mic, "Regimen" = regimen, "Stratified by" = cov,
    "Stratum" = stratum, "Published day" = published, "Simulated day" = crit,
    "Difference (days)" = diff_days
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The simulated critical days track Table S1 across both regimens, both MICs and
all strata. The eGFR strata agree to within about three days, at most ten
percent of the published day. The weight strata run consistently later than
published, by roughly two to nine days (up to about 15%), and more so after the
third dose. The paper does not report how weights were distributed within each
stratum (a uniform draw is used here), which would explain a shift confined to
the weight strata. An error in clearance or its eGFR exponent would move the
eGFR strata as well, and an error in a weight exponent would grow with distance
from the 79 kg reference, whereas the shift is about as large in the 50-79 kg
stratum as in the 120-200 kg one.

```{r tableS1-check}
summary(chk$diff_days)
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed clearance, exponent or reference value shifts
  # every stratum by a week or more.
  abs(median(chk$diff_days)) <= 4,
  # Envelope: robust to which strata land in the Monte Carlo tails.
  quantile(abs(chk$diff_days), 0.9) <= 12
)
```

# Typical-value profiles

```{r typical}
typ_cov <- tibble::tibble(
  label = c("eGFR 20, 79 kg", "eGFR 75, 79 kg", "eGFR 110, 79 kg", "eGFR 75, 50 kg", "eGFR 75, 140 kg"),
  CRCL = c(20, 75, 110, 75, 75),
  WT = c(79, 79, 79, 50, 140)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(), dose_times = list(c(0, 7 * hours_per_day)))
ev_typ <- make_events(typ_cov)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(typ_cov, id, label), by = "id")

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(time / hours_per_day, Cc, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Total dalbavancin (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical patients, 1500 mg on day 1 and day 8"
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

Sayadi 2026 reports no non-compartmental analysis, so the NCA below is an
internal consistency check on the packaged model. A single 1500 mg dose is
simulated in 50 eGFR-stratified patients per stratum (with between-subject
variability) over 100 days. PKNCA reads a thinned grid -- 2-hourly over the
first two days, 12-hourly to day 14, then daily -- because NCA on the full 2-h
grid over 100 days is needlessly slow.

```{r nca}
n_nca <- 50L
nca_cohort <- cohort |>
  dplyr::filter(regimen == "D1/D8", cov == "eGFR") |>
  dplyr::group_by(stratum) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = n_nca) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::mutate(dose_times = list(0))
ev_sd <- make_events(nca_cohort)
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_sim, ev_sd, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(nca_cohort, id, stratum), by = "id")

nca_times <- c(seq(0, 48, by = 2), 0.5, seq(60, 14 * hours_per_day, by = 12), seq(15 * hours_per_day, 100 * hours_per_day, by = 24))
conc_sd <- sim_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time %in% nca_times) |>
  dplyr::select(id, stratum, time, Cc)
conc_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  conc_sd,
  dplyr::distinct(conc_sd, id, stratum) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, stratum, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

dose_sd <- ev_sd |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::select(nca_cohort, id, stratum), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::select(id, stratum, time, amt)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_sd, Cc ~ time | stratum + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_sd, amt ~ time | stratum + id),
  intervals = data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
    aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
))

as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(stratum, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  dplyr::mutate(half.life = half.life / hours_per_day) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "eGFR stratum" = stratum, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "AUC0-inf (mg*h/L)" = aucinf.obs, "Terminal half-life (days)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

For a linear model eliminating only from the central compartment, AUC to
infinity after one intravenous dose equals dose divided by the subject's
clearance. This per-subject identity checks the PKNCA set-up and the
simulation grid together.

```{r nca-identity}
auc_check <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::select(id, aucinf = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::distinct(sim_sd, id, cl), by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_error = 100 * (aucinf - 1500 / cl) / (1500 / cl))
stopifnot(nrow(auc_check) == 4L * n_nca)
summary(auc_check$pct_error)
# Same drawn parameters on both sides: the only difference is trapezoid and
# extrapolation error on the thinned grid, so a tight bound holds for every
# subject.
stopifnot(max(abs(auc_check$pct_error)) < 2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate equation.** The Methods equation for continuous covariates is
  typeset as `log(theta_i) = log(theta_pop) + log(theta_cov) x (Cov_i /
  Cov_median)`, which is not a power function. The surrounding text ("tested
  using power functions (allometric scaling)"), the Table 4 footnote ("beta,
  covariate effect (power exponent)") and the fixed volume exponents of 1 all
  describe the Monolix power form `theta_i = theta_pop x (Cov_i /
  Cov_median)^beta`, which is used here. The Table S1 reproduction above
  confirms this reading.
* **Reference covariate values.** The paper centres on the "population median"
  without printing it in the covariate equations; the Table 2 medians (79 kg,
  75 mL/min/1.73 m^2) are used. Table 2 summarises the observed values, before
  k-nearest-neighbour imputation of the 15-16% missing weights and creatinine
  values, so the median Monolix used may differ slightly.
* **eGFR column.** The paper's CKD-EPI eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2) is supplied in
  the `CRCL` column, the package's canonical name for BSA-normalised renal
  function.
* **Random effects.** Table 4 reports omega as the standard deviation of the
  log-normal random effect (CV% 17.5 for omega 0.17, i.e. sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1));
  the variances in `ini()` are the squared SDs. No correlations between random
  effects were reported, so the omega matrix is diagonal.
* **Unbound fraction.** `fu = 0.07` and the unbound output `Ccu` are not part
  of the fitted model; they reproduce the paper's conversion for the PTA
  simulations.
* **PTA simulation details not reported.** The within-stratum covariate
  distribution is drawn uniformly; the third dose is given at the end of the
  stratum's critical day; fAUC24 is computed per calendar day by the linear
  trapezoid on a 2-h grid without residual error. The paper's Methods state that
  RUV was applied in the Monte Carlo simulations but not how it entered the
  AUC; it is omitted here. Cohorts are 200 per stratum instead of 10,000.
* **Comparator models and model averaging** are not packaged with this model
  (see Model and source).
